Rashi on Yevamot 20b:14:1.english: A decree [prohibiting] the first [act of] intercourse - through which he fulfills a positive commandment and is able to override [the prohibition].

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:14:2.hebrew: אטו ביאה שניה - דלא מצי למידחי, דהא איקיים בה עשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:14:2.english: Due to a second [act of] intercourse - For it cannot override [the prohibition], since the positive commandment has already been fulfilled through her.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:16:1.hebrew: לאו מילתא היא דאמרי - דבביאה ראשונה הויא שרי לכתחילה אי לאו משום גזירת ביאה שניה; דודאי אפילו ביאה ראשונה אסורה, ולא אמרי' תדחה עשה את לא תעשה, דהא אפשר להתקיים בחליצה בלא עקירת לא תעשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:16:1.english: That which I said is not correct - [Namely,] that regarding the first act of intercourse, it would be permitted initially were it not for the decree [concerning] a second act of intercourse; for certainly even the first act of intercourse is forbidden, and we do not say [that] the positive commandment overrides the prohibition, since it is possible [for it] to be fulfilled through ḥalitza without uprooting the prohibition.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:17:1.english: If they engaged in intercourse, they acquired [her] - Thus, by Torah law, she falls before him [for levirate marriage] to override a negative commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:17:2.hebrew: תיובתא - דרבא ותיובתא דריש לקיש, דאמרי לעיל, אם אתה יכול לקיים את שניהם, לא עקרנא ליה ללאו:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:17:2.english: A conclusive refutation - of Rava and a conclusive refutation of Reish Lakish, who said above: "If you can fulfill both of them, I do not uproot the negative prohibition."

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:18:2.hebrew: פוטרת - אותה ואת צרתה מן החליצה, וסגי לה בגט:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:18:2.english: Exempts - [it exempts] her and her rival wife from chalitzah, and a get [bill of divorce] suffices for her.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:1:1.hebrew: תפסי בה קידושין - הילכך קרינן ביה "לקחת" בדיעבד. אבל חייבי כריתות לא תפסי בהו קידושין, ואפי' עבר האי יבם ונסבה, לאו קיחה היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:1:1.english: Betrothal takes effect with her - Therefore, we apply to him [the verse's term] "to take" after the fact. However, [with those] liable for karet, betrothal does not take effect with them, and even if this yavam transgressed and married her, it is not [considered] a "taking."

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:3:1.hebrew: לצדדין קתני בא עליה - קאי אאיסור מצוה, דהיינו שניות מדברי סופרים, דמדאורייתא חזיא ליה וקמיה רמיא, לפיכך נפטרה צרתה בביאתה. חלץ — קאי אאיסור קדושה, דרמיא לחליצה, הילכך חליצתה פוטרת צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:3:1.english: [The baraita] teaches it disjunctively; "[If] he engaged in intercourse with her" - [This] refers to a prohibition [resulting from] a mitzva, that is, secondary [prohibited relations] by rabbinic decree, for by Torah law she is fit for him and falls before him [for levirate marriage]; therefore, her rival wife is exempt through her intercourse. "[If] he performed ḥalitza" — [this] refers to a prohibition [stemming from] sanctity, for she is subject to ḥalitza; therefore, her ḥalitza exempts her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:1.english: A man with crushed testicles and one whose penis has been severed - Later [the Gemara] explains them in the chapter [entitled] He'arel.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:2.hebrew: סריס אדם - שסירסו אדם, ולא מחמת חולי נסתרס מאליו. והוי בלאו, דבכלל פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה הוא, ואסור לישא ישראלית, דכתיב: "לא יבא פצוע דכא":
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:2.english: A eunuch [caused] by man - [This means one] whom a person castrated, and [who] did not become castrated on his own due to illness. And he is subject to a negative commandment, for he is included in [the category of] "one with crushed testicles or whose penis is severed," and he is forbidden to marry an Israelite woman, as it is written: "One with crushed testicles shall not enter [the assembly of the Lord]."

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:3.hebrew: והזקן - שפסק מלידה. והאי לאו מחייבי לאוין הוא, אלא קמ"ל דאע"ג דלאו בר אולודי הוא, ביאתו ביאה לקנות יבמתו, ויוצאה ממנו בגט:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:3.english: And the elderly man - Who has ceased [to be able] to procreate. And this [man] is not among those liable for [violating] negative commandments; rather, [the Tanna] teaches us that even though he is not capable of begetting children, his intercourse is [valid] intercourse to acquire his yevamah, and she leaves him with a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:4.hebrew: או מייבמין - לאו לכתחלה קאמר, אלא ייבומן יבום, שאם בעלו קנו, כדקתני ואזיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:4.english: Or they perform levirate marriage - It does not mean [that they may do so] initially, rather [that] their levirate marriage is [a valid] levirate marriage, for if they engaged in intercourse, they acquired [her], as it goes on to teach.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:5.hebrew: ונתנו גט - כלומר, או נתנו גט או חלצו. וגט ביבמה מהני למיפסל עליו ועל כל האחין, דאי בעי לייבומי תו לא מצי, דקם ליה בשוב לא יבנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:5.english: And gave a bill of divorce - That is to say, either they gave a bill of divorce or they performed ḥalitza. And a bill of divorce in [the case of] a yevama is effective to disqualify [her] to him and to all the brothers, so that if he wants to perform levirate marriage, he can no longer [do so], since he is subject to [the rule of] "he shall not build again."

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:4:6.english: And if they engaged in intercourse, they acquired [them] - And they are released with a bill of divorce without ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:5:1.hebrew: ואסור לקיימן - אסיפא קאי: מתו אחין ובעלו הן את יבמתן, ואפצוע דכא וכיוצא בו, ולאו אזקן:
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:5:1.english: And it is forbidden to maintain them - [This] refers to the latter clause: "[If] the brothers died and they had intercourse with their yevamot"; and [it refers] to one with crushed testicles and the like, and not to an elderly man.

Rashi on Yevamot 20b:6:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - חייבי לאוין נמי לייבום רמיא, הלכך אם בעלו קנו. ודקשיא לך: באלמנה ארוסה שנפלה לכהן גדול, תתייבם ויבא עשה וידחה את ל"ת — אלמנה מן האירוסין נמי כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 20b:6:1.english: Rather, Rava said - Women forbidden by a negative prohibition are also subject to levirate marriage; therefore, if they cohabited, they have acquired [her as a wife]. And as for what you asked: in the case of a betrothed widow who fell [for levirate marriage] before a High Priest, let her perform levirate marriage and let the positive commandment come and override the negative prohibition — [Rava answers that] a widow from betrothal is also [both a positive commandment and a negative prohibition], etc.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:13:1.hebrew: אי הכי כל הנשים לא יתייבמו - כל הני פירכי לא פריך שיעקרו חכמים לגמרי מצות ייבום, והכי פי': "אשת אחיו מאביו לא תתייבם" — כשאינו אחיו אלא מאביו, לא תתייבם עד דמיחדי באבא ובאמא, גזיר' משום אשת אחיו מאמו. "אשה שאין לה בנים לא תתייבם" — פירוש: שאין לה עכשיו, אבל היו לה בחיי הבעל ומתו, גזירה משום אשה שיש לה בנים. "אשת אחיו שהיה בעולמו" — כגון שבא ממדינת הים והיה מוחזק לן דלית ליה אחים, דדמי כמי שלא היה בעולמו. "כל הנשים לא יתייבמו" — פירוש: אשה שלא היה לה בנים מעולם, לא מזה ולא מאחר, דדמיא לאילונית:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:13:1.english: If so, none of the women should enter into levirate marriage - [In] all of these objections, [the Gemara] is not asking that the Sages should completely uproot the mitzvah of levirate marriage; rather, this is its explanation: "The wife of his brother from his father should not enter into levirate marriage" — when he is only his brother from his father, she should not enter into levirate marriage unless they share both a father and a mother, [as] a decree due to the wife of his brother from his mother. "A woman who has no children should not enter into levirate marriage" — meaning, one who has none now, though she had [children] during [her] husband's lifetime and they died, [as] a decree due to a woman who has children. "The wife of his brother who was in his world" — for example, where he came from overseas and it was presumed by us that he had no brothers, so that he resembles one who was not in his world. "None of the women should enter into levirate marriage" — meaning, a woman who has never had children, neither from this [husband] nor from another, for she resembles an aylonit.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:14:1.hebrew: גזירה ביאה ראשונה אטו כו' - אלמנה מן הנשואין וחייבי עשה — נפקא לן מיבמתו, דאע"ג דאין עולין ליבום, עולין לחליצה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:14:1.english: "The first [act of] intercourse is a decree due to etc." - [Regarding] a widow from [full] marriage [to a High Priest] and those [prohibited by] a positive commandment: we derive from [the verse] "his yevamah" that even though they do not enter into yibum, they [nevertheless] enter into chalitzah.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:14:2.hebrew: אטו ביאה שניה - לאו דוקא נקט ביאה שניה, דהא אפילו גמר ביאה ראשונה אסור, דיבמה נקנית בהעראה, והו"מ למימר "גזירה אטו גמר ביאה". ואין להתיר ביאה שניה מטעם דנעשית אשתו לכל דבר, דאינה נעשית כאשתו אלא היכא דשרי ליה בלא דחייה, אבל חייבי לאוין — אפילו ביאה ראשונה לא שריא אלא משום דאתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה, וביאה שניה דלית בה עשה לא דחיא. אע"ג דבפרק הבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות סא.) לא מצריך קרא אלא לאירס ואח"כ נתמנה להיות כהן גדול, אבל נשאה קודם שנתמנה משמע דלא צריך קרא, שיכול לקיימה משום דנשאה בהיתר — התם נמי משום דבהיתר בלא שום דחיית איסור נשאה, אבל הכא ביאה ראשונה לא שריא אלא משום דאתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה; ביאה דמצוה דחיא, דלאו מצוה לא דחיא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:14:2.english: Due to a second [act of] intercourse - [The Gemara] did not specifically mean a second [act of] intercourse, for even the completion of the first [act of] intercourse is prohibited, since a yevama is acquired through the initial stage of intercourse [ha'ara'ah], and [the Gemara] could have said, "[It is] a decree due to the completion of [the first act of] intercourse." And one cannot permit the second [act of] intercourse on the grounds that she has become his wife in all respects, because she only becomes like his wife where she is permitted to him without overriding [a prohibition]. However, [in the case of] those obligated in negative prohibitions [ḥayavei lavin] — even the first [act of] intercourse is only permitted because a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative commandment, whereas the second [act of] intercourse, in which there is no positive commandment, does not override [the prohibition]. Even though in the chapter "Haba al Yevimto" (later, Yevamot 61a), [the Gemara] only requires a verse for [a case where] he betrothed [a widow] and was subsequently appointed to be High Priest, while [if] he married her before he was appointed, it implies that a verse is not needed, [as] he may remain married to her because he married her permissibly — there too, [it is] because he married her permissibly without any overriding of a prohibition; however, here, the first [act of] intercourse is only permitted because a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative commandment; [thus,] an act of intercourse that is a mitzvah overrides [the prohibition], [while one] that is not a mitzvah does not override [it]:

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:17:1.hebrew: מיתיבי ואם בעלו קנו - תימה, דרבא גופי' מותיב מהך ברייתא, והשתא איתותב מינה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:17:1.english: "They raised an objection: And if they engaged in intercourse, they acquired [her]" - It is astonishing, for Rava himself raises an objection from this baraita, and now he is refuted by it.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:1:1.hebrew: מסתברא חייבי לאוין תפסי בהו קדושין - ותימה: מנלן לאוקמי קרא בחייבי לאוין? נוקי קרא בחייבי עשה גרידא, דאע"ג דאין מייבמין, מ"מ עולים לחליצה כיון דתפסי בהו קידושין; אבל חייבי לאוין — נימא דאתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה ויעלו גם לייבום! וי"ל דמשמע ליה השתא לדרוש מקרא ד"יבמתו" לאסור יבום ולהצריך חליצה. אבל קשה: א"כ, היכי הוה בעי לאוקמי קרא בחייבי כריתות? והא ל"ל דהכי פריך: ואימא חייבי כריתות נמי ליבעי חליצה מהאי קרא? דהא קאמר בתר הכי "ומה ראית", דמשמע "ואימא איפכא":
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:1:1.english: "It stands to reason: [for] those liable for [violating] negative commandments, betrothal takes effect" - And this is puzzling: From where do we [know] to establish the verse as referring to those liable for negative commandments? Let us establish the verse as referring solely to those liable for positive commandments — for although they do not perform levirate marriage, nevertheless they are subject to ḥalitza since betrothal takes effect with them; but [as for] those liable for negative commandments — let us say that the positive commandment [of levirate marriage] comes and overrides the negative commandment, and they should be subject to levirate marriage as well! And one can answer that it seems to [the Gemara] now [that we should] expound from the verse "his yevama" to forbid levirate marriage and to require ḥalitza. However, this is difficult: If so, how could [the Gemara] have wanted to establish the verse as referring to those liable for karet? And one cannot say that it is asking thus: "Say that those liable for karet also require ḥalitza from this verse," because it says after that: "And what did you see [to conclude thus]?", which implies: "Say the opposite!"

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:4:1.hebrew: פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה וסריס אדם - פירוש: סריס אדם לאפוקי בידי שמים, שלא היה להם שעת הכושר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:4:1.english: A man with crushed testicles, one whose penis has been severed, and a eunuch [caused] by man - Explanation: "A eunuch [caused] by man" is to exclude [a eunuch] by the hand of Heaven, who never had a time of fitness:

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:4:2.hebrew: אם בעלו קנו - ה"ה דלכתחילה נמי שרי, כדמוכח לקמן; אלא איידי דנקט בסיפא לשון דיעבד, נקט נמי ברישא לשון דיעבד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:4:2.english: "If they engaged in intercourse, they acquired [them]" - The same applies [even] initially, that it is also permitted, as is proven below; rather, since [the Tosefta] used an ex post facto formulation in the latter clause, it also used an ex post facto formulation in the former clause.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:7:1.hebrew: אמר קרא והתקדשתם - אע"ג דהאי עשה נמי הוה במצות יבום ואיכא תרי עשה, מ"מ אין תרי עשה דוחה ל"ת ועשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20b:7:1.english: The verse states, "Sanctify yourselves" - Even though this positive commandment also applies to the mitzvah of levirate marriage, and [thus] there are two positive commandments, nevertheless two positive commandments do not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment.
